question: What are the general architecture, training pipeline, model landscape, benchmark performance and open directions of MultiModal LLMs (MM-LLMs) built by augmenting off-the-shelf LLMs?
contributions: Comprehensive coverage of nearly all MM-LLMs of the past year, around 120 or more, including understanding and generative models, beyond VL to audio and 3D point cloud
A general model architecture of five components with any-to-any modality transformations, with the implementation choices for each
A summary of developmental trends of MM-LLMs and training recipes that improve effectiveness
An open-source tracking website (https://mm-llms.github.io) with crowdsourced updates

limits: Authors concede that some aspects may have eluded scrutiny and recent advances may not be fully captured; they rely on a crowdsourced tracking website to keep up.
Page limits meant concise overviews of core contributions only, not all technical details.
Benchmark table (Table 2) copies numbers from different papers with different protocols; asterisk marks training images seen, so cross-model comparison is not controlled.
Only 4 of 18 benchmarks (OKVQA, IconVQA, VQAv2, GQA) are discussed; the survey does not run any experiment itself.
Coverage ends around Feb 2024 (v5 May 2024); later models (for example natively multimodal frontier models) have dated it.
Table 2 has no statistical uncertainty, no compute or cost columns, and no audio or 3D results.
practices: Keep modality encoder, LLM backbone and modality generator frozen and train mostly the input and output projectors (Section 2).
Use PEFT (prefix-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, LayerNorm tuning) on the LLM backbone when more adaptation is needed; trainable parameters stay under 0.1% (Section 2.3, Appendix C).
Two-stage pipeline: MM pre-training on X-text pairs to align projectors, then MM instruction tuning (SFT then optionally RLHF) (Section 3).
Use a higher image resolution (336 or 448, or tile or compress tokens) when fine-grained detail matters, and watch the token-length cost (Section 5).
Add high-quality SFT data such as ShareGPT4V (Section 5).
Prefer interleaved image-text data over image-text pairs only for pre-training, and re-blend text-only instruction data during SFT to avoid text-only degradation (Section 5, from VILA).
Simpler input projectors (linear or MLP) work as well as Q-Former or P-Former; Q-, P-, MQ-Former need extra PT for initialisation (Sections 2.2 and 4 trend 5).
For any-to-any generation, use off-the-shelf latent diffusion models as generators (Stable Diffusion, Zeroscope, AudioLDM-2) conditioned through an output projector (Section 2.5).
Tool-using designs treat the LLM as a black box with expert systems; end-to-end designs avoid propagated errors in the cascade (Introduction and Section 4).

terms.definition: MultiModal Large Language Models that augment off-the-shelf LLMs to support MM inputs or outputs via cost-effective training strategies
tasked with encoding inputs from diverse modalities IX to obtain corresponding features FX, FX = MEX(IX)
tasked with aligning the encoded features of other modalities FX with the text feature space T; trained by minimising the X-conditioned text generation loss
processes representations from various modalities, producing direct textual outputs t and signal tokens SX for other modalities
maps the signal token representations SX from the LLM Backbone into features HX understandable to the following Modality Generator; trained with an MSE loss to the generator's text-condition encoder
tasked with producing outputs in distinct modalities, commonly off-the-shelf Latent Diffusion Models, trained with the conditional LDM loss
pre-training stage where Input and Output Projectors are trained on X-Text datasets to align modalities
fine-tuning of pre-trained MM-LLMs using instruction-formatted datasets, comprising SFT and RLHF
Tool-using denotes treating the LLM as a black box and providing access to certain MM expert systems; End-to-End signifies the entire model is trained jointly
extracts relevant features from FX with learnable queries; the selected features are used as prompts PX
uses a set of trainable vectors as queries and the encoded features as keys to compress the feature sequence to a fixed length
assumes the parameter change lies in a low-rank space; h = Wx + deltaW x = Wx + ABx with r much smaller than min(c,d)
